title: Core starter kit
description: What packages/core contains, optional modules, and when to use optional sync.

blocks.text: packages/core is not a runtime dependency. It is a generic boilerplate copied once when you run pnpm new-template. After that, the template folder is a complete Next.js app — all imports resolve locally with @/.

blocks.title: No template names in core
blocks.text: Core must stay vertical-agnostic: no hotel pages, no real-estate models, no client brand copy. Only reusable auth, leads, storage, health, and shared UI pieces.

rows: Minimal app/layout.tsx, app/page.tsx, app/globals.css (theme CSS bridge), THEME.md, GETTING_STARTED.md from packages/core/scaffold/

blocks.text: What is NOT copied by default

items: Hero, Footer, enquiry modal — optional core modules (hero-simple, footer, enquiry-modal)
SEO pack, gallery CMS, reviews, legal pages — optional modules (seo, gallery, reviews, legal-pages)
Home page composition — scaffold placeholder or wired by --modules
Domain listing grids and vertical APIs — template modules or hand-built features

blocks.text: Cross-vertical features live in packages/core/modules/ and are registered in packages/core/modules.json. Install at creation with --modules or later with pnpm template:add-module (monorepo) or tempjs add-module (client projects).

rows: Light/dark toggle, colorsDark, globals [data-theme=dark], layout hydration guards

blocks.text: New scaffolds and every sync/new-template run ensureTemplateThemeGlobals: :root vars from constants/site.ts, Tailwind v4 @theme tokens, body wired to CSS variables (no inline SITE.theme.colors on <html>). Repair one template with pnpm template:theme-globals <id> or all with pnpm template:theme-globals.
Full install workflow, template vertical modules, and planned admin tab registry: see Optional modules page.

blocks.code:
pnpm new-template bakery bakery-website-template --name "Bakery Website"
pnpm new-template bakery --modules enquiry-modal,footer,hero-simple,seo,gallery,reviews

blocks.text: If you fix a bug in packages/core and want existing templates to receive it without hand-copying files:
Normal template development does not use sync. Use pnpm template:diff-core before propagate to see what would change.
